name: Resident Permit -- Marriage to a Citizen

qualifying_event.description: The spouse of an Antiguan and Barbudan citizen may apply for a Resident Permit after at least 1 year of marriage.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Marriage certificate; proof of the citizen spouse's nationality; proof of cohabitation.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires being married to an Antiguan and Barbudan citizen for at least 1 year.
requirements.fix_path: Reach 1 year of marriage to the citizen spouse.

requirements.blocker_text: Applicant must not have been convicted of a serious offence.

evidence_required.document: Health certificate and proof of insurance

outcome.duration_length: 3 years, unless a shorter period is specifically applied for; renewable

sources.title: Immigration Department, Antigua and Barbuda -- Residency Permit FAQs: marriage ground, 1 year after marrying a citizen; general-services/residency page corroborates with the same 1-year figure and adds that residency can be revoked and reapplied for within 3 months upon death or divorce
Immigration Department, Antigua and Barbuda -- Residency general-services page: marriage-to-citizen ground (1 year), revocation and 3-month reapplication window on death/divorce

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Antigua and Barbuda's initial build. Modelled as a separate 'family' category file from ag_resident_permit_general.json (which covers the general/student/independent-means/entrepreneur grounds, all 'settled') even though both are the same underlying Resident Permit under the Immigration and Passport Act 2014 -- split follows this dataset's convention of separating routes by category where the schema materially differs by ground. Distinct downstream route: a marriage-based Resident Permit holder can additionally register directly for citizenship after 3 years of marriage and cohabitation under ag_citizenship_by_marriage.json, a faster path than the general 7-year Resident Permit-to-citizenship figure also modelled here as a fallback. Per the general-services page, if the marriage ends in death or divorce, the Resident Permit can be revoked, but the (former) spouse may reapply within 3 months under the standard (non-marriage) eligibility grounds -- flagged here rather than modelled as a separate route, since it is a contingency on this same route rather than a distinct entry point.
